draft.title: Stalin's Soviet Union
card: Stalin became the unchallenged leader of the Soviet Union in the late 1920s after Lenin's death. He removed rivals from the Communist Party and built a personal dictatorship.
Cult of personality
the state presented Stalin as a wise, all-knowing leader. His image and name filled posters, newspapers, films and place names.
Forced industrialisation

from 1928, Five Year Plans set high targets for heavy industry such as coal, steel and machinery. The state ran the economy and farms were collectivised, meaning peasants were pushed into state-controlled farms.
Terror

the secret police arrested people said to be enemies, some of them real opponents and many of them innocent. The Great Purge of the 1930s used show trials, labour camps and executions, and it also hit the Party, the army and ordinary people.
draft.remember: Stalin ruled through three tools: an image of a great leader, state-driven industry, and fear of arrest.

a.q: Why did the Great Purge of the 1930s help Stalin keep his dictatorship?
opts: Fear of arrest, even for the innocent, discouraged opposition
It gave Party members more say in running the country
It replaced the secret police with elected courts
It ended the Five Year Plans and let peasants own farms
a.why: The purges targeted real and imagined enemies, so nobody felt safe enough to challenge Stalin. The idea that it gave Party members more say is wrong, because even senior Party members were arrested.
a.clue: Think about what people did when anyone could be arrested.

b.q: In 1937 a Soviet factory manager is arrested and shown in a show trial, and his name is removed from the factory walls. Posters across the country praise Stalin as the leader who guides all workers. What do these two events together show?
opts: Terror and a cult of personality both supported Stalin
Forced industrialisation had ended and his rule was weak
Stalin shared power with the managers of Soviet industry
The cult of personality was meant to shield people from arrest
b.why: The trial shows terror against supposed enemies, and the posters show the cult of personality. Both built Stalin's power at the same time. The idea that managers shared power is wrong, because a manager was arrested and put on trial.
b.clue: One event is about fear and the other is about image.
